_how_to_use: Fill in `canonical` BEFORE translating anything. One term, one rendering, for the whole language.
verify.py enforces it: if a source field mentions the term on the left, the translation must contain the value on the right.
Leave a value empty to switch that check off.
`watch_variants` is for spellings that drifted in a previous language. Add any you catch; verify.py reports when more than one is used.
`overrides` switches the canonical-term check off for one field, when the ENGLISH source is itself wrong. Give a reason.

overrides.categories.name.2: English says "Dua's Excellence", but this category holds Tasbeeh/Tahmid/Tahlil/Takbeer, and the Bengali says dhikr. Translated as dhikr.
overrides.duas.translation.285: English asks for a successor among the deceased's descendants. The supplied Arabic واخلفه في عقبه and Bengali ask Allah to take care of those left behind; Urdu follows that meaning without repeating the Bengali's duplicated grave supplication.
overrides.duas.translation.294: English adds '(of faith)' to the reward. The supplied Arabic أجره refers to the deceased, as the Bengali also indicates; Urdu preserves that reference without the unsupported English parenthesis.
overrides.duas.translation.295: English renders وعافه as 'give him strength'. The supplied Arabic and Bengali ask for well-being or safety; Urdu uses عافیت عطا فرما.
overrides.duas.translation.297: English calls the deceased the son of a male and female servant. The supplied Arabic عبدك وابن أمتك calls him Allah's servant and the son of His female servant; the Bengali supports this, and Urdu follows it.
overrides.duas.translation.299: As in row 295, Arabic wa aafihaa and Bengali mean well-being, not strength. The stray English masculine pronouns refer to the female deceased; Urdu consistently uses the female context.
overrides.duas.translation.301: English calls her the daughter of male and female servants. Supplied Arabic and Bengali call her Allah's female servant and the daughter of His female servant; Urdu follows those.
overrides.duas.note.310: English asks whether to pray on Laylatul Qadr. Bengali asks what supplication to make, which matches the response teaching a particular dua; Urdu follows Bengali.
overrides.duas.note.315: English adultery is too narrow. Bengali describes sexual conduct, and Bukhari 1894 uses la yarfuth; Urdu preserves the broader meaning. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:1894 .
overrides.duas.translation.316: English describes past actions, but the Arabic and Bengali are a supplication for the hosts; Urdu retains that prayer form.
overrides.duas.name.319: English title mentions only returning, but the main dua and content concern starting a journey and the nested group adds the return wording. Urdu follows the Bengali title covering both.
overrides.duas.translation.321: English safety represents Arabic amanataka; Bengali explicitly says entrusted responsibility. Urdu uses the established religious term amanat.
overrides.duas.note.321: The explanatory rendering repeats the same amanataka phrase as the main translation; Urdu consistently uses amanat rather than English safety. Embedded Latin transliteration remains verbatim.
overrides.duas.name.323: English title says traveller praying for resident, but the actual dua and note concern arriving or stopping at a place. Urdu follows the Bengali subject; retains English #1.
overrides.duas.name.324: English title says traveller praying for resident, but the actual dua and note concern entering a town. Urdu follows the Bengali subject; retains #2.
overrides.duas.content.327: Abu al-Malih is the intermediary narrator, not the Companion who rode behind the Prophet. Use rahimahullah for him and radiyallahu anhu for the unnamed Companion. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4982 and https://sunnah.com/narrator/4091 .
overrides.duas.note.327: Same narrator attribution and honorific correction as content. Preserve the repeated narration and the note's additional ending.
overrides.duas.translation.329: English capitalizes He Who listens ambiguously. Bengali addresses a hearer, matching Arabic samia samiun; Urdu addresses the listener and does not turn this into a divine name.
overrides.duas.note.331: English says any means of transport, contradicting the boat title and dua. Bengali specifically says land vehicles; Urdu follows that scope while preserving the author's statement.
overrides.duas.content.339: English marks Amr ibn Shuayb as a Companion and vaguely says predecessors. Preserve the chain through his father to his grandfather, use rahimahullah for Amr and radiyallahu anhu for the Companion, and identify preceding prophets as in Bengali and Tirmidhi 3585. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3585 .
overrides.duas.note.339: Same chain, honorific and preceding-prophets correction as content; preserve the repeated narration.
overrides.duas.group_items.343.1.note: English incorrectly inserts (the sky) as the subject and says full fair. This is the Prophet staying until daylight brightens, as the parallel narration in row 340 and Bengali show.
overrides.duas.content.347: Both supplied prose versions corrupt the animal and body-part description. The cited Bukhari 5565 explicitly describes two horned black-and-white rams and placing a foot on their sides. Urdu restores those details. Checked https://sunnah.com/bukhari:5565 .
overrides.duas.content.352: Muslim occurs only in the inline citation [Muslim: 780], which the skill requires copying in English. Do not add an Urdu collection name solely to satisfy the canonical-term check.
overrides.duas.note.357: The Uqbah here is Uqbah ibn Muslim, an intermediary narrator in Abu Dawud 466, not the Companion Uqbah ibn Amir. Use rahimahullah rather than the source RA. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:466 .
overrides.duas.content.361: Source Husain (RA) is an attribution error. Hisn al-Muslim attributes these words to Hasan al-Basri; Urdu uses Hasan Basri rahimahullah. Checked https://risala.prh.gov.sa/storage/contents/51/ar_hisnulmuslim.pdf . The frozen Abu Dawood: 441 reference is retained for a separate source audit.
overrides.duas.content.367: Surah occurs only in the inline reference, which is retained verbatim in English per the skill. Do not add an Urdu surah label to the narrative solely for the glossary check.
overrides.duas.note.368: English duplicates the rooster narration in the second paragraph. Bengali and the actual second reference, Abu Dawud 5103, concern dogs and donkeys at night; Urdu follows those, retaining [1] and [2]. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5103 .
overrides.duas.translation.370: English Messenger is singular, whereas the supplied Arabic rusulihi and Bengali are plural. Urdu correctly says His messengers.
overrides.duas.note.372: Abu Zumayl is the intermediary narrator reporting his question to Ibn Abbas, not a Companion. Urdu uses rahimahullah for him and radiyallahu anhuma for Ibn Abbas. Checked https://sunnah.com/abudawud:5110 .
overrides.duas.translation.379: English repent for me is incorrect for tub alayya, which asks Allah to accept repentance. It also swaps the wrong divine name: supplied Arabic and Bengali replace Rahim with Ghafur while retaining Tawwab.
overrides.duas.note.380: English middle of the night omits the qualifying last part. Bengali and Arabic Tirmidhi 3579 say the last part of the night. The heart wording follows the restrained covering metaphor also used in row 389. Checked https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:3579 .
overrides.duas.content.387: English pray is imprecise: Bengali and the repeated Bukhari 6307 wording ask forgiveness and repent. Urdu explicitly preserves both actions.
overrides.duas.content.388: Arabic Muslim 2702b says al-Agharr was narrating TO Ibn Umar, not quoting FROM him. Abu Burdah is the intermediary narrator, so use rahimahullah. Checked https://sunnah.com/muslim:2702b .
overrides.duas.content.389: English goes astray overstates the meaning. Bengali describes momentary preoccupation; Urdu preserves the covering metaphor of layughanu ala qalbi, matching the parallel narration in row 380. Arabic independently checked at https://sunnah.com/muslim:2702a .
overrides.duas.content.390: English wrongly introduces the displayed text as the prayer tashahhud. The supplied text is Khutbat al-Hajah, as Bengali says. Preserve the initial mention of both teachings but introduce the correct displayed passage.
overrides.duas.translation.390: English omits the kinship clause from Quran 4:1. Supplied Arabic wal-arham and Bengali both include it; Urdu restores it without altering citation numbers.
overrides.duas.translation.394: English and Bengali mistranslate the final clause as gathering or separating good things. Supplied Arabic asks Allah to keep the spouses together in goodness for as long as He joins them, and to separate them in goodness if He separates them.
overrides.duas.translation.412: English omits by Your favour, which is explicit in the supplied Arabic bifadlika and Bengali. Urdu preserves this phrase.
overrides.duas.translation.416: English repeats the grave trial and says wash my sins. Supplied Arabic and Bengali have one grave-trial clause and ask to wash the heart with snow and hail water. Urdu follows those without the English duplication.
overrides.duas.translation.417: English omits Lord of the earth, which appears in the supplied Arabic and Bengali. Restore it in Urdu and render the present grasp of the forelock rather than the English future tense.
overrides.duas.note.365: English reverses the wording of the hypothetical regret. Bengali and Muslim 2664 say if I had done such-and-such, this would have happened. Urdu preserves that conditional form.
overrides.duas.note.381: The prose omits the speaker. Musnad Ahmad 712 explicitly has Ali reporting that the Prophet addressed him; restore that attribution. Retain the unusual already-forgiven wording, which really occurs in the Arabic. Checked the Musnad text reproduced at https://dorar.net/h/JcEng0hJ?osoul=1 .
overrides.duas.content.394: The cited Adab al-Zifaf discusses a raised report but explicitly prefers the version stopping at Ibn Masud. Attribute this instruction to Ibn Masud rather than unconditionally to the Prophet; frozen reference remains unchanged. Checked https://islamhouse.com/read/ar/????-??????-??-?????-???????-276162 , section 2, footnote to the second report.
overrides.duas.note.397: The supplied claim about Companions conflicts with the Hasan al-Basri attribution in row 396 and the Nawawi recommendation for the reply in row 362. Urdu uses the accurate broader attribution to scholars; see Hisn al-Muslim chapter 47, https://risala.prh.gov.sa/storage/contents/51/ar_hisnulmuslim.pdf .

_notes: Categories and subcategories were translated from the English WITH the Bengali (reference_bn) beside it.
Where the two disagree the Bengali was followed, because it matches what the category actually contains.
Example: category 2 is "Dua's Excellence" in English but holds Tasbeeh/Tahmid/Tahlil/Takbeer, which is dhikr - the Bengali says dhikr, so the Urdu says ذکر.
Example: category 37 is "Prophet's Dua" in English but contains the duas of Adam, Ayyub and Yunus (AS) - the Bengali plural was followed: انبیاء و رُسل.
